title: Ben McMillan - Attack of the Liquid Alternative Clones (S2E3)

reader_summary.headline: A word of mouth is how this podcast grows.
reader_summary.overview: A word of mouth is how this podcast grows. Ben, we're going to give it a little count. In this episode, I chat with Ben McMillan, a founding partner of IDX Insights, a firm offering custom indexing as a service.

key_points.text: Ben cut his teeth and we spend a considerable amount of time discussing how this experience impacted his research in building hedge fund replication strategies..
key_points.evidence_quote: Ben cut his teeth and we spend a considerable amount of time discussing how this experience impacted his research in building hedge fund replication strategies.

key_points.text: As it turns out, a naive replication strategy is very easy to implement.
key_points.evidence_quote: As it turns out, a naive replication strategy is very easy to implement.

key_points.text: A robust one, however, is deceptively difficult.
key_points.evidence_quote: A robust one, however, is deceptively difficult.

key_points.text: One of the most interesting insights I gleaned from this conversation is that the edge in replication may not be in applying more sophisticated math.
key_points.evidence_quote: One of the most interesting insights I gleaned from this conversation is that the edge in replication may not be in applying more sophisticated math, but rather in the data sets applied.

thesis: The episode explores the difficulty of accurately replicating hedge fund strategies using liquid instruments like ETFs, noting that while naive replication is easy, robust replication is deceptively difficult. The discussion highlights that the edge in replication may lie in the data sets applied rather than more sophisticated math, and examines the dependent nature of liquid replicators on their less liquid peers.
